how_this_was_measured: P16-01 recorded the type position as UNKNOWN because 'mypy did not complete'. It aborted on `Source file found twice under different module names` — and EXITED 0. Run with --explicit-package-bases --namespace-packages it completes. P16-R6 recorded 703 errors over 869 source files in CI. P14-R3 RATCHETED IT DOWN to 701: FINDING AQ's fix replaced two `attr-defined` errors in api/routes/webhooks.py (owner_connection is annotated as yielding `object`, so every method call on it is an error) with one typed local. The file count rises to 877 with the files P14-R1..R3 added; unlike the error count it does not move with the environment, because it is a property of the tree. P17-01 RAISED THE FLOOR to 878: tests/tenancy/test_p17_evaluate_harness.py is one more file in the tree. The floor is the half of this ratchet that stops a falling error count being mistaken for improvement, so it has to be tightened whenever the tree grows — a floor left behind is a floor that would not notice the same number of files disappearing again. P17-02 raised it again to 879 for tests/tenancy/test_p17_system_benchmark.py. P17-03 raised it to 880 for the ratchet test file and the benchmark test file. B2 raised the floor to 884 for the four source files this batch adds: core/billing/provider.py, core/billing/subscriptions.py and the two new test modules. The CEILING is unchanged at 701 — the thirteen attr-defined errors the new modules would otherwise have added were removed with typed locals, the same fix P14-R3 used, rather than by loosening the ratchet. B1/B2 RATCHETED THE CEILING DOWN to 698. The billing modules did not add errors — the typed locals removed three more than they introduced, the same fix P14-R3 and B2 both used — and the ratchet is what said so: it FAILED at 701 with 'the ceiling must come down', which is the direction this gate is supposed to fail in and the reason it is a ratchet rather than a threshold. The number is CI's, read from the reference environment's own output; the development environment measures 700 over the same 884 files, the same delta of 2 recorded when this baseline was written at 705/703, and it is not the number enforced. Reading it at all required FINDING CH: verify-type-gate.sh took its measurement through a pipeline under `set -euo pipefail`, so the gate's non-zero exit killed the self-test before it printed anything, and CI reported 'the type gate self-test failed' about a gate that was working. fix/memory-per-user RATCHETED THE CEILING DOWN to 697. Moving erase_vectors' leftover count into a helper that takes the connection as a parameter removed one attr-defined error (workspace_connection is annotated as yielding `object`), the same kind of fix as P14-R3's; the ratchet FAILED at 698 with 'the ceiling must come down', and CI measured 697. fix/realtime-memory RATCHETED THE CEILING DOWN to 696. One of the 697 was the realtime brain's defect itself: `IraMemorySink.remember` called `memory.store.remember` without its `principal`, which mypy reported as `Missing positional argument "content"` [call-arg] while every brain memory write raised TypeError at run time. Fixing the call removed it. Measured in the development environment as a delta of one over the same tree (664 on main, 663 with the fix); the enforced number is CI's. fix/memory-contradiction-check RATCHETED THE CEILING DOWN to 695, after fix/realtime-memory's 696. One of the 696 was the contradiction check's defect itself: `memory/temporal.py::check_before_save` called `retrieve_active` without its `principal`, which mypy reported as `Missing positional argument "query" in call to "retrieve_active"` [call-arg] while every check raised TypeError at run time. Fixing the call removed it. Measured in the development environment as 697 on main and 696 with this fix alone over the same 1050 files, and 695 with both fixes merged; the enforced number is CI's.
reference_environment: CI, and ONLY CI. The error count moves with the installed packages — mypy resolves attributes against the modules it can import. This gate was written against a development environment measuring 705; CI, which installs only requirements-test.txt, measured 703. Neither is wrong; they are answers about different environments. A ratchet over a number that moves with the environment is not a ratchet, so the ceiling is recorded from CI and enforced there. Elsewhere the gate reports the measurement and enforces only what is environment-independent: that mypy FINISHED, and that it analysed the files on disk.
what_this_is: A RATCHET, not a threshold. max_errors may only ever come down: exceeding it fails, and dropping below it also fails, with instructions to lower the number. A ratchet that is not tightened is a threshold, and a threshold drifts back.
why_min_files_checked_exists: A FALLING ERROR COUNT IS NOT EVIDENCE OF IMPROVEMENT. It is equally consistent with a module no longer being analysed — an import that now fails, a directory excluded, a module-scope `# type: ignore`, or a rename that takes a file out of the discovered set. Each makes the number better and the position worse. A drop here fails regardless of the error count.
